problem: Existing high-level VLN benchmarks such as REVERIE use single-goal instructions and short episodes, so they do not capture real-world multi-objective, long-horizon navigation where information from earlier sub-goals could be reused.
motivation: Real-world robots (lifelong, long-horizon) must carry out sequences of high-level instructions and should exploit environment information gathered during earlier sub-goals. This calls for a benchmark and a study of long-term memory and which knowledge types best enrich it.
key_idea: Introduce the MG-VLN benchmark (multi-goal, long-horizon extension of REVERIE) and a language-enhanced long-term memory map that stores visual content plus linguistic knowledge (categories, captions, attributes/relationships) gathered in previous sub-goals.
insight: According to the abstract, an explicit long-term memory map substantially improves navigation in multi-goal, long-horizon settings. Among the linguistic knowledge types, object attributes and relationships are the most helpful for aligning environmental cues with high-level instructions. Detailed ablations were not available (abstract only).
method: MG-VLN benchmark: extends REVERIE to sequences of multiple high-level instructions (multi-goal) with long navigation horizons, in simulation.
Long-term memory map: an explicit map that accumulates environmental information observed during previous sub-goals for reuse in later ones.
Language-enhanced memory: augments visual content in the map with linguistic knowledge such as object categories, visual captions, and object attributes/relationships.
Knowledge-type study: compares which kinds of linguistic knowledge best align the memory with high-level instructions.

setting.training_data: not specified in abstract (built on REVERIE-derived data)
setting.observation: not specified in abstract (visual observations with object information)

results: The abstract reports qualitative findings only: an explicit long-term memory map significantly enhances navigation in multi-goal, long-horizon scenarios, and object attributes/relationships are the most beneficial knowledge type. No numbers are given.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so implementation details and metrics could not be verified.
Benchmark is simulation-only and built on REVERIE.
